plan: This is a first-price sealed-bid auction, but with a twist: the winner pays the second-highest bid. This is a Vickrey auction variant. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy, meaning it's the best strategy regardless of what the other bidders do. Bidding below my value risks losing profit if I could have won for less, and bidding above my value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. Since this is the first and only round, there's no history to learn from, so I'll stick to the dominant strategy.

Given my value of $28, and knowing this is a single-round game, I will bid slightly above my expected payment if I win. In a second-price auction, a common strategy is to bid your true value. However, since I pay the second-highest bid, I can potentially bid slightly higher than my value to increase my chances of winning, as long as the second-highest bid is below my value. I will bid 28.1 to slightly edge out a true-value bidder.

I will bid slightly above my true value to increase my chances of winning while still ensuring a profit. Given my value is $14, I will bid $14.10. This strategy is robust against other rational bidders and aims to maximize long-term profit by winning when profitable and minimizing losses.
